title: Parallax Operation Algebra (m-op-algebra)
description: Canonical, format-agnostic serialization of an m-op-algebra operation node. Each node is a single-key tagged object. The temporal algebra addresses axes by the closed dimensions `valid-time` and `transaction-time`: `asOf` carries `dimension` plus `coordinate`, `asOfRange` carries `dimension` plus finite `start`/`end`, and `history` carries `dimension`. An omitted Transaction-Time selection normalizes to explicit Latest; Valid Time must be selected explicitly on a bitemporal read. An explicit Latest coordinate is serialized as `latest`; finite coordinates are ordinary timestamps, with no `Now` variant. Physical interval predicates are injected by m-temporal-read and never authored in the operation. The remaining nodes cover the full predicate, relationship, nested-value-object, result-directive, and inheritance-narrowing algebra.

attributeRef.description: A metamodel attribute reference of the form Entity.attribute, whose Entity segment is bare or namespace-qualified (identity.schema.json).

relationshipRef.description: A metamodel relationship reference of the form Entity.relationship, whose Entity segment is bare or namespace-qualified (identity.schema.json).

pathSegment.description: One hop in a deep-fetch navigation path: a CLOSED object naming the relationship to traverse via `rel` (a `Class.relationship` reference) and OPTIONALLY narrowing that hop's polymorphic target with `narrow`. The object shape is the single structural carrier for a hop, so a POLYMORPHIC hop (a relationship whose target is an abstract root / abstract subtype, m-inheritance) may carry `narrow` alongside `rel` without a second spelling of a path. A broad hop (no `narrow`) populates the ORDINARY relationship view keyed by the local relationship name; a narrowed hop populates a DISTINCT narrowed view keyed `<rel>[<Concrete>,<Concrete>]` (the effective concrete set, canonical alphabetical order by entity name, no spaces — m-deep-fetch), and does NOT mark the broad relationship loaded. Deduplication of equivalent spellings applies BETWEEN TWO NARROWED hops: two authored `narrow.to` lists resolving to the same effective set (`[Pet]` vs `[Cat, Dog]`) derive the SAME view key and deduplicate to one hop. A broad hop and ANY authored narrow over the same relationship are DISTINCT hops — including a REDUNDANT narrow, one resolving to the relationship target's ENTIRE effective concrete set, which returns exactly the broad hop's rows yet populates the bracketed view key rather than the ordinary one. Hop identity at a segment therefore keys on whether a narrow was AUTHORED as well as on the effective set it resolves to.

pathNarrow.description: The subtype narrowing of ONE deep-fetch hop: constrain the relationship's polymorphic target to a Subtype Selection (m-inheritance). The position is the relationship's target (implicit) and there is no inner predicate, because a hop eagerly fetches a whole VIEW rather than filtering. Validation resolves the selection inside the relationship target's effective concrete set (`narrow-outside-relationship-target` otherwise, m-navigate / m-deep-fetch).

navigationPath.description: ONE path to eager-fetch: a CLOSED object carrying the hops to traverse under its required `segments` member, e.g. { segments: [{ rel: 'Order.items' }] } (one hop) or { segments: [{ rel: 'Order.items' }, { rel: 'OrderItem.product' }] } (multi-hop), plus the OPTIONAL path-root `narrow` that guards which queried objects the path starts from. `segments` is an ordered, NON-EMPTY list read left to right from the queried entity, each entry a closed object (`pathSegment`) rather than a bare string, so broad and narrowed hops share one uniform shape; a polymorphic hop MAY carry `narrow` (subtype narrowing of that hop's target). The object — rather than a bare segment array — is the single structural carrier for a path, so what qualifies the path as a whole stays distinguishable from what qualifies one hop. The two narrow positions are deliberately OPPOSITE: the path-root narrow (`pathRootNarrow`) guards SOURCE objects and creates NO view key, while a segment narrow (`pathNarrow`, on a `pathSegment`) narrows one hop's TARGET and creates a distinct narrowed view.

pathRootNarrow.description: The Subtype Selection guarding a deep-fetch path's ROOT position: restrict the path to queried objects in the resolved selection without changing the read's own result set (m-inheritance, m-deep-fetch). The root position is supplied by context, exactly like the operation-position narrow; a guard resolving outside it is `narrow-outside-position` and one resolving to nothing is `narrow-empty-effective-set`. A root guard creates NO view key: every hop populates the same ordinary (or segment-narrowed) view on fewer root objects. Hop identity at the root position keys on the resolved source set alone.

literal.description: A scalar literal value usable as a bind.

stringMatch.description: A string predicate. `value` is a plain string; `like`/`notLike` interpret `%`/`_` as wildcards, the affix forms (startsWith/endsWith/contains) treat `value` as a literal and the implementation escapes wildcards. `caseInsensitive` defaults to false.

group.description: An explicit precedence-nesting node. It wraps a single inner operation so that a fluent or prefix surface that intends to group a sub-expression serializes to one unambiguous canonical form.

orderBy.description: A result-shaping directive: order an inner query's rows by one or more keys.

nulls.description: Where NULLs sort on this key, independent of `direction`. Omitted means `last`, the canonical default in both directions. Placement is observable only on a nullable attribute; on a non-nullable one both placements lower to the same term.

limit.description: A result-shaping directive: cap an inner query's row count.

navigationFilter.description: Filter the queried entity by traversing a relationship. `rel` names the relationship; the optional `op` constrains the related entity. With no `op` it is a pure existence check.

navigate.description: navigate(rel) -> predicate: filter via traversal to a related entity. Lowers to a correlated EXISTS semi-join, so a to-many navigation never multiplies parent rows.

exists.description: exists(rel[, op]): the queried entity has at least one related row (optionally matching `op`). Lowers to a correlated EXISTS.

notExists.description: notExists(rel[, op]): the queried entity has no related row (optionally matching `op`). Lowers to a correlated NOT EXISTS.

deepFetch.description: An eager-fetch directive: resolve the inner query, then fetch each named navigation path with ONE additional statement per relationship level (N+1 elimination). The result is an object graph, not a flat row set.

narrow.description: narrow(to, operand): constrain the POLYMORPHIC position supplied by context to a Subtype Selection (m-op-algebra, m-inheritance). At top level the position is the read's targetEntity; inside a navigation filter it is the relationship target; inside another narrow it is the enclosing selection's resolved set. `operand` is evaluated over the narrowed position. Model-aware validation resolves the selection, requires a non-empty subset of the active position, and threads that resolved set into `operand`; SQL lowering lifts the narrow into tag/branch selection (m-sql).

temporalCoordinate.description: A temporal point: the literal `latest` or a finite ISO-8601 UTC instant. There is no `Now` coordinate or `now` wire alias.

finiteTemporalInstant.description: A finite ISO-8601 UTC instant; `latest` and `now` are not valid range bounds.

asOf.description: asOf(dimension, coordinate): pin one temporal dimension to Latest or a finite instant. Latest lowers to end = infinity; a finite instant lowers to interval containment. Omitted Transaction Time normalizes to an explicit Latest wrapper; omitted Valid Time is invalid on a bitemporal read. A bitemporal operation nests one wrapper per dimension in Valid-Time-then-Transaction-Time order.

asOfRange.description: asOfRange(dimension, start, end): scan a temporal dimension across a finite half-open instant range, returning every milestone that overlaps [start, end).

history.description: history(dimension): return the full milestone set for a temporal dimension. No as-of predicate is injected on that dimension.

nestedRef.description: A reference into a valueObject's inner field: an Entity spelling (bare or namespace-qualified, identity.schema.json) and its valueObject followed by one or more dotted path segments into the embedded document (e.g. Customer.address.city, Customer.address.geo.lat). Lowers to a dialect-specific text extraction on the value object's backing column (m-sql/m-dialect).

nestedComparison.description: A nested-field comparison: a valueObject inner attribute (referenced by a dotted path) compared against a TYPED literal. The `path` resolves against the model's declared valueObject structure (first segment a declared valueObject on the entity, intermediates nested valueObjects, leaf a declared attribute); the `value` is a polymorphic `literal` whose type MUST match the leaf attribute's declared type (m-op-algebra). The dialect-specific document extraction (m-sql/m-dialect) casts to that declared type before comparing.

nestedRange.description: A nested-field range test: a valueObject inner attribute (referenced by a dotted path) bounded below and above by TYPED literals. The `path` resolves against the model's declared valueObject structure (as for `nestedComparison`); BOTH bounds are `literal`s whose type MUST match the leaf attribute's declared type (m-op-algebra). A `lower` strictly greater than its `upper` names an empty range and MUST be rejected (m-op-algebra bound-ordering rule), checked AFTER the typed-literal rule so a mistyped bound is named as such. Lowers to one `<extraction> between ? and ?` — never two comparisons — with the JSON path bind(s) first, then `lower`, then `upper` (m-sql/m-dialect).

nestedMembership.description: A nested-field membership test: a valueObject inner attribute (referenced by a dotted path) tested against a non-empty list of TYPED literals. The `path` resolves against the model's declared valueObject structure (as for `nestedComparison`); each list value is a `literal` whose type MUST match the leaf attribute's declared type (m-op-algebra). Lowers to `<extraction> in (?, ?, …)` — negated with a leading `not` for `nestedNotIn` — with the JSON path bind(s) first, then one bind per list value in order (m-sql/m-dialect).

nestedStringMatch.description: A nested-field string predicate: a valueObject inner attribute (referenced by a dotted path) matched against a pattern or a literal affix. The `path` resolves against the model's declared valueObject structure (as for `nestedComparison`) and its leaf's declared type MUST be `String`; a string predicate aimed at any other member is `nested-string-predicate-non-string-member`, checked BEFORE the typed-literal rule so a `date` / `time` / `timestamp` / `uuid` / `bytes` member — which rides the portable string literal and so would otherwise pass the typed-literal check — is named rather than silently accepted (m-op-algebra). `value` carries the top-level `stringMatch` semantics unchanged: `%` and `_` are wildcards for `nestedLike` / `nestedNotLike`, while the affix forms (`nestedStartsWith` / `nestedEndsWith` / `nestedContains`) treat it as literal text whose wildcards the implementation escapes. `caseInsensitive` defaults to false and otherwise folds BOTH sides with `lower(...)`. Lowers to `<extraction> like ?` — `<extraction> not like ?` for `nestedNotLike`, the same infix negation the scalar `notLike` renders — with the JSON path bind(s) first, then the pattern, then the escape character when escaping actually changed the literal (m-sql/m-dialect).

nestedNullCheck.description: A nested-field presence test: a valueObject inner attribute referenced by a dotted path, with NO compared value. The `path` resolves against the model's declared valueObject structure (as for `nestedComparison`). Per the absence-collapse rule (m-op-algebra) every 'not present' state — SQL NULL column, missing key, JSON `null`, non-object intermediate segment — yields SQL NULL from the extraction, so `nestedIsNull` matches exactly those rows and `nestedIsNotNull` its complement.

nestedEq.description: nestedEq(path, value): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute equals a typed literal.

nestedNotEq.description: nestedNotEq(path, value): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute differs from a typed literal.

nestedGt.description: nestedGt(path, value): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is greater than a typed literal (the extraction is cast to the declared type before comparing).

nestedGte.description: nestedGte(path, value): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is greater than or equal to a typed literal.

nestedLt.description: nestedLt(path, value): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is less than a typed literal.

nestedLte.description: nestedLte(path, value): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is less than or equal to a typed literal.

nestedBetween.description: nestedBetween(path, lower, upper): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute lies within an inclusive range of two typed literals. One canonical node, never two comparisons — through a `many` segment a SINGLE element must satisfy the whole range.

nestedIn.description: nestedIn(path, values): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is one of a non-empty list of typed literals.

nestedNotIn.description: nestedNotIn(path, values): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is NOT one of a non-empty list of typed literals. Through a `many` segment this keeps the uniform any-element reading — SOME element's member is not in the list — exactly as nestedNotEq does; the no-element reading is spelled nestedNotExists(path, where: nestedIn(…)).

nestedLike.description: nestedLike(path, value, caseInsensitive?): filter where an embedded valueObject String attribute matches a SQL pattern — `%` and `_` are wildcards and the pattern passes through unescaped.

nestedNotLike.description: nestedNotLike(path, value, caseInsensitive?): the negation of nestedLike, lowered as the infix `not like`. Through a `many` segment it keeps the uniform any-element reading — SOME element's member does not match the pattern.

nestedStartsWith.description: nestedStartsWith(path, value, caseInsensitive?): filter where an embedded valueObject String attribute begins with the LITERAL text `value`, whose own wildcards are escaped before the trailing `%` is appended.

nestedEndsWith.description: nestedEndsWith(path, value, caseInsensitive?): filter where an embedded valueObject String attribute ends with the LITERAL text `value` (escaped, then prefixed with `%`).

nestedContains.description: nestedContains(path, value, caseInsensitive?): filter where an embedded valueObject String attribute contains the LITERAL text `value` (escaped, then wrapped in `%`).

nestedIsNull.description: nestedIsNull(path): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is 'not present' (SQL NULL column, missing key, JSON null, or non-object intermediate — all collapsed per m-op-algebra).

nestedIsNotNull.description: nestedIsNotNull(path): filter where an embedded valueObject attribute is present (the complement of nestedIsNull).

valueObjectRef.description: A path that TERMINATES at a valueObject member (not an inner attribute): an Entity spelling (bare or namespace-qualified, identity.schema.json) and its valueObject, optionally followed by nested valueObject segments (e.g. Customer.address, Customer.address.phones). Unlike `nestedRef` — which requires an ATTRIBUTE leaf and so carries at least two member segments — this path may carry just one, because its subject is the value OBJECT itself. It resolves against the declared structure (first member segment a declared valueObject on the entity, each further segment a nested valueObject declared on the preceding member); the final member's multiplicity (`one` / `many`) selects the presence vs non-empty semantics of nestedExists/nestedNotExists (m-op-algebra).

elementRef.description: An ELEMENT-RELATIVE path used ONLY inside a scoped `where` (nestedExists/nestedNotExists over a `many` member). It carries NO Entity spelling — the subject is the array element bound by the enclosing exists — so it is one or more lowercase-initial dotted segments naming declared members of that element (`type`, `number`, or `geo.country` to descend a nested value object of the element). Each segment resolves against the element's declared structure (intermediates nested valueObjects, leaf a declared attribute).

elementComparison.description: An element-scoped nested comparison: an element-relative `path` compared against a TYPED literal whose type MUST match the leaf attribute's declared type. The subject is the array element bound by the enclosing nestedExists/nestedNotExists `where`.

elementRange.description: An element-scoped nested range test: an element-relative `path` bounded below and above by TYPED literals whose type MUST match the leaf attribute's declared type. One element must satisfy the WHOLE range, and the bound-ordering rule applies exactly as it does path-scoped.

elementMembership.description: An element-scoped membership test: an element-relative `path` tested against a non-empty list of typed literals.

elementStringMatch.description: An element-scoped string predicate: an element-relative `path` whose leaf's declared type MUST be `String`, matched against a pattern (`nestedLike` / `nestedNotLike`) or a literal affix (the three affix forms), with the same wildcard, escaping, and `caseInsensitive` semantics the path-scoped form carries.

elementNullCheck.description: An element-scoped presence test: an element-relative `path` with NO compared value.

elementPredicate.description: A scoped sub-predicate evaluated against ONE array element inside a nestedExists/nestedNotExists `where`. It is the flat `nested*` family re-expressed over element-relative paths (`elementRef`), composed with the ordinary boolean combinators. The whole compound must be satisfied by a SINGLE element (same-element semantics), which is what distinguishes it from ANDing flat any-element predicates at the top level (m-op-algebra).

nestedExistsBody.description: The body of nestedExists/nestedNotExists: a value-object-terminated `path` and an OPTIONAL element-scoped `where`. Without `where` the meaning is presence — a `one` member present (non-absent per the absence-collapse rule), a `many` member a NON-EMPTY array. With `where` (a `many` path), ONE element must satisfy the whole compound `where` sub-predicate (same-element semantics); nestedNotExists + where means NO element satisfies it (m-op-algebra). Lowers to the m-dialect array-traversal form (m-sql).

nestedExists.description: nestedExists(path[, where]): the value object at `path` is present (`one`) or its array is non-empty (`many`); with `where`, at least one element satisfies the compound sub-predicate.

nestedNotExists.description: nestedNotExists(path[, where]): the complement of nestedExists — the value object is absent (`one`) or the array is empty/absent (`many`); with `where`, no element satisfies the compound sub-predicate.
